# Script template injection best practices (2026-01-27 21:09Z)

_**User**_

This custom code @scripts/generate-static-pages.js:92-178for each page seems like a bad practice.

Is there a better way to inject this  script template markup?

It should be done with the @views/partials/scripts.html or another one for the bottom of the page.

There should be a cleaner best practice for this?

Provide some solutions

        "contents": "function getPageInitScript(routeKey, isProduction) {\n&#96;;\n    }\n    \n    // All other pages use View class\n    return &#96;&lt;script type=\"module\"&gt;\n  import { View } from '${basePath}pages/View.js';\n  import { whenDOMReady } from '${basePath}utilities/AsyncHelpers.js';\n  import { $ } from '${basePath}utilities/DOMHelpers.js';\n  import { ATTRIBUTES } from '${basePath}utilities/Constants.js';\n  \n  whenDOMReady(async () =&gt; {\n    // Read the template from the main element to determine the element selector\n    const main = $(\"main[data-template]\");\n    const template = main?.getAttribute(ATTRIBUTES.DATA_TEMPLATE);\n    \n    if (!template) {\n      console.error(\"No data-template attribute found on main element\");\n      return;\n    }\n    \n    // Create element selector from template (e.g., \"section-1\" -&gt; \".section-1\")\n    const elementSelector = '.' + template;\n    \n    // Get services from App.js (or create if App.js hasn't loaded yet)\n    let services = window.appServices;\n    if (!services) {\n      const { createServices } = await import('${basePath}services/ServiceFactory.js');\n      services = createServices();\n    }\n    \n    // Initialize page with the template-based element selector\n    const page = new View({\n      element: elementSelector,\n      ...services,\n    });\n    await page.create();\n    await page.show();\n  });\n&lt;/script&gt;&#96;;\n  }\n\n  // Ensure dist directory exists\n  await mkdir(outputDir.pathname, { recursive: true });\n\n  // Find all HTML files in pages directory\n  const glob = new Glob(\"**/*.html\");\n\n  for await (const file of glob.scan(viewsPagesDir.pathname))\n}",

        "contents": "/**\n * SiteConfig - Site-wide route mappings and page metadata\n * Harmonizes the data-template field to href, js classes and browser urls \n * Central configuration for all routes, page classes, and transition data\n */\n\nimport { siteRoutes } from './siteRoutes.js';\n\nexport class SiteConfig {\n  constructor() {\n    this.routes = {};\n    this.initializeSettings();\n  }\n\n  initializeSettings() {\n    this.settings = siteRoutes;\n  }\n\n  get(template) {\n    return this.settings[template];\n  }\n\n  getClass(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.class;\n  }\n\n  getLink(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.link;\n  }\n\n  getUrl(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.url;\n  }\n\n  getTemplate(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.template;\n  }\n\n  has(template) {\n    return this.settings[template] !== undefined;\n  }\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./documentation/guides/COMPONENT_GUIDE.md",
        "range": {

        },
        "contents": "  async onBeforeCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeShow() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterShow() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeHide(route) {} // Optional\n  async onAfterHide(route) {} // Optional\n  onBeforeDestroy() {} // Optional\n  onAfterDestroy() {} // Optional\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Subclass Using Hooks\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Home.js\nexport class Home extends Page {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      id: \"home\",\n      element: \".home\",\n      elements: { /* ... */ },\n    });\n  }\n  \n  // ✅ Only define hooks you need\n  async onAfterCreate() {\n    // Custom logic after page is created\n    this.setupHomeSpecificFeatures();\n  }\n  \n  async onAfterShow() {\n    // Custom logic after page is shown\n    this.playWelcomeAnimation();\n    this.initializeHomeSlider();\n  }\n  \n  async onBeforeHide(route) {\n    // Custom cleanup before hiding\n    this.stopHomeAnimations();\n  }\n}\n\n// View.js - No hooks needed, uses parent implementation\nexport class View extends Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    super({ id, element, elements });\n  }\n  // ✅ Doesn't need to define anything - uses parent's show/hide\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Composition vs Inheritance\n\n### Current: Inheritance\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass Page {\n  async show() { /* ... */ }\n}\n\nclass Home extends Page {\n  // Home IS-A Page\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Alternative: Composition\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page is a composition of behaviors\nclass Page {\n  constructor(behaviors = {}) {\n    this.showBehavior = behaviors.show || new DefaultShowBehavior();\n    this.hideBehavior = behaviors.hide || new DefaultHideBehavior();\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.showBehavior.execute(this);\n  }\n}\n\n// Home uses composition\nclass Home {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      show: new HomeShowBehavior(), // Custom behavior\n      hide: new DefaultHideBehavior(), // Default behavior\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Inheritance vs Composition Comparison\n\n### Inheritance (Current Approach)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Simple - familiar pattern\n- ✅ Direct access to parent methods\n- ✅ Good for \"IS-A\" relationships (Home IS-A Page)\n- ✅ Less boilerplate\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Tight coupling - subclass depends on parent",

            "text": "  async onBeforeHide(route) {",
            "lineNumber": 3713
          },
          {
            "text": "    // Custom cleanup before hiding",
            "lineNumber": 3714
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.stopHomeAnimations();",
            "lineNumber": 3715
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 3716
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3717
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3718
          },
          {
            "text": "// View.js - No hooks needed, uses parent implementation",
            "lineNumber": 3719
          },
          {
            "text": "export class View extends Page {",
            "lineNumber": 3720
          },
          {
            "text": "  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {",
            "lineNumber": 3721
          },
          {
            "text": "    super({ id, element, elements });",
            "lineNumber": 3722
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 3723
          },
          {
            "text": "  // ✅ Doesn't need to define anything - uses parent's show/hide",
            "lineNumber": 3724
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3725
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3726
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3727
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 3728
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3729
          },
          {
            "text": "## Composition vs Inheritance",
            "lineNumber": 3730
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3731
          },
          {
            "text": "### Current: Inheritance",
            "lineNumber": 3732
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3733
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 3734
          },
          {
            "text": "class Page {",
            "lineNumber": 3735
          },
          {
            "text": "  async show() { /* ... */ }",
            "lineNumber": 3736
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3737
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3738
          },
          {
            "text": "class Home extends Page {",
            "lineNumber": 3739
          },
          {
            "text": "  // Home IS-A Page",
            "lineNumber": 3740
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3741
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3742
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3743
          },
          {
            "text": "### Alternative: Composition",
            "lineNumber": 3744
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3745
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 3746
          },
          {
            "text": "// Page is a composition of behaviors",
            "lineNumber": 3747
          },
          {
            "text": "class Page {",
            "lineNumber": 3748
          },
          {
            "text": "  constructor(behaviors = {}) {",
            "lineNumber": 3749
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.showBehavior = behaviors.show || new DefaultShowBehavior();",
            "lineNumber": 3750
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.hideBehavior = behaviors.hide || new DefaultHideBehavior();",
            "lineNumber": 3751
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 3752
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 3753
          },
          {
            "text": "  async show() {",
            "lineNumber": 3754
          },
          {
            "text": "    await this.showBehavior.execute(this);",
            "lineNumber": 3755
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 3756
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3757
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3758
          },
          {
            "text": "// Home uses composition",
            "lineNumber": 3759
          },
          {
            "text": "class Home {",
            "lineNumber": 3760
          },
          {
            "text": "  constructor() {",
            "lineNumber": 3761
          },
          {
            "text": "    super({",
            "lineNumber": 3762
          },
          {
            "text": "      show: new HomeShowBehavior(), // Custom behavior",
            "lineNumber": 3763
          },
          {
            "text": "      hide: new DefaultHideBehavior(), // Default behavior",
            "lineNumber": 3764
          },
          {
            "text": "    });",
            "lineNumber": 3765
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 3766
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 3767
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 3768
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3769
          },
          {
            "text": "## Inheritance vs Composition Comparison",
            "lineNumber": 3770
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3771
          },
          {
            "text": "### Inheritance (Current Approach)",
            "lineNumber": 3772
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3773
          },
          {
            "text": "**Pros:**",
            "lineNumber": 3774
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Simple - familiar pattern",
            "lineNumber": 3775
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Direct access to parent methods",
            "lineNumber": 3776
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Good for \"IS-A\" relationships (Home IS-A Page)",
            "lineNumber": 3777
          },
          {
            "text": "- ✅ Less boilerplate",
            "lineNumber": 3778
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3779
          },
          {
            "text": "**Cons:**",
            "lineNumber": 3780
          },
          {
            "text": "- ❌ Tight coupling - subclass depends on parent",
            "lineNumber": 3781
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.3583582639694214
    },

        "contents": "                  officials acting independently.\n                &lt;/div&gt;\n              &lt;/section&gt;\n            &lt;/a&gt;\n            &lt;a\n              data-directional-hover-item=\"\"\n              href=\"#footnote-101\"\n              class=\"page-footnotes__item footnote-link\"\n            &gt;\n              &lt;div class=\"page-footnotes__border\"&gt;&lt;/div&gt;\n              &lt;section class=\"page-footnotes__footnote\" id=\"footnote-101\"&gt;\n                &lt;div class=\"page-footnotes__footnote-number\"&gt;101&lt;/div&gt;\n                &lt;div class=\"page-footnotes__footnote-detail\"&gt;\n                  The Forward's source in the March article also said the five\n                  men were released (Suter had fled to Israel) because \"they did\n                  not know anything about 9/11.\" But this statement needs to be\n                  weighed in the light of the men's demeanor and statements, and\n                  the statements of local law enforcement officials, on\n                  September 11, 2001, the inclusion of Mr. Suter on the May 2002\n                  FBI Suspect List, and the revelations on that List that Hudson\n                  and Bergen Counties were a critical center of operations for\n                  the future hijackers and FBI suspects as noted above. The FBI\n                  was also under pressure from U.S. political figures to release\n                  the members of the Israeli New Jersey Group, including Richard\n                  Armitage of the State Department and two New York Congressmen.\n                  Senior U.S. Officials Join Effort To Free 5 Israelis Held in\n                  Brooklyn, Ha'aretz News, October 29, 2001.\n                &lt;/div&gt;\n              &lt;/section&gt;\n            &lt;/a&gt;\n            &lt;div class=\"page-footnotes__border\"&gt;&lt;/div&gt;\n          &lt;/div&gt;\n        &lt;/section&gt;\n      &lt;/section&gt;\n    &lt;/main&gt;\n\n    &lt;footer class=\"footer\"&gt;\n      &lt;div class=\"footer__content\"&gt;\n        &lt;p class=\"footer__text footer__text--highlight\" data-animation=\"title\"&gt;\n          ",

          {

            "text": "                  the future hijackers and FBI suspects as noted above. The FBI",

{
  "plan": "# Refactor Page Initialization Scripts to Templates\n\n## Current Problem\nThe &#96;getPageInitScript()&#96; function in &#96;scripts/generate-static-pages.js&#96; generates inline scripts as strings, mixing JavaScript logic with template generation. This violates separation of concerns and makes maintenance harder.\n\n## Solution Options\n\n### Solution 1: Nunjucks Partial with Conditionals (Recommended)\nCreate &#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96; that uses Nunjucks conditionals to render the appropriate script based on &#96;pageClass&#96; and &#96;basePath&#96; template variables.\n\n**Changes:**\n- Create &#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96; with conditional blocks for Home, Introduction, and View\n- Update &#96;views/layouts/page.html&#96; to include the partial instead of using &#96;pageScript&#96; variable\n- Modify &#96;scripts/generate-static-pages.js&#96; to:\n  - Remove &#96;getPageInitScript()&#96; function\n  - Pass &#96;pageClass&#96; and &#96;basePath&#96; as template variables instead of &#96;pageScript&#96;\n  - Use the &#96;class&#96; property from &#96;siteRoutes&#96; config\n\n**Pros:**\n- Keeps template logic in templates\n- Easy to read and maintain\n- Leverages existing Nunjucks infrastructure\n\n**Cons:**\n- Some duplication in template conditionals\n\n### Solution 2: Data-Driven Single Script\nCreate a single initialization script that reads page metadata from data attributes on the &#96;&lt;main&gt;&#96; element, eliminating the need for page-specific scripts.\n\n**Changes:**\n- Create &#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96; with a single script that:\n  - Reads &#96;data-page-class&#96; attribute from &#96;&lt;main&gt;&#96; element\n  - Dynamically imports the appropriate page class\n  - Handles all initialization logic in one place\n- Update page templates to add &#96;data-page-class&#96; attribute\n- Modify &#96;scripts/generate-static-pages.js&#96; to:\n  - Remove &#96;getPageInitScript()&#96; function\n  - Pass &#96;pageClass&#96; as template variable\n  - Update page templates to include the attribute\n\n**Pros:**\n- Single script, no duplication\n- More flexible and extensible\n- Cleaner separation (logic in JS, data in HTML)\n\n**Cons:**\n- Requires runtime attribute reading\n- Slightly more complex JavaScript\n\n### Solution 3: Nunjucks Macro\nCreate a reusable macro file for page initialization scripts.\n\n**Changes:**\n- Create &#96;views/macros/page-init.njk&#96; with a macro that accepts &#96;pageClass&#96; and &#96;basePath&#96;\n- Create &#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96; that calls the macro\n- Update &#96;scripts/generate-static-pages.js&#96; similar to Solution 1\n\n**Pros:**\n- Most reusable approach\n- Follows DRY principles\n\n**Cons:**\n- Adds abstraction layer (may be overkill for 3 cases)\n- Requires macro file structure\n\n## Recommended Approach\n**Solution 1** is recommended because:\n1. It's the simplest migration path\n2. Keeps template logic visible and maintainable\n3. Leverages existing Nunjucks patterns in the codebase\n4. Easy to understand for future developers\n\n## Implementation Details (Solution 1)\n\n### Files to Create/Modify:\n\n1. **Create &#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96;**\n   - Use &#96;{% if pageClass === \"Home\" %}&#96;, &#96;{% elif pageClass === \"Introduction\" %}&#96;, &#96;{% else %}&#96; blocks\n   - Each block renders the appropriate script with &#96;{{ basePath }}&#96; variable\n\n2. **Modify &#96;views/layouts/page.html&#96;**\n   - Replace &#96;{% if pageScript %}{{ pageScript | safe }}{% endif %}&#96; with &#96;{% include \"partials/page-init.html\" %}&#96;\n\n3. **Modify &#96;scripts/generate-static-pages.js&#96;**\n   - Remove &#96;getPageInitScript()&#96; function (lines 93-178)\n   - Add &#96;pageClass&#96; to &#96;templateData&#96; using &#96;routeConfig.class&#96; from SiteConfig\n   - Add &#96;basePath&#96; to &#96;templateData&#96; (already computed)\n   - Remove &#96;templateData.pageScript&#96; assignment\n\n4. **Update page templates** (if needed)\n   - Ensure &#96;data-template&#96; attribute exists (already present)\n\n## Benefits\n- Separation of concerns: template logic in templates, not JavaScript\n- Easier maintenance: script changes don't require modifying build script\n- Better readability: scripts visible in template files\n- Consistent with existing partial pattern (&#96;scripts.html&#96;, &#96;footer.html&#96;, etc.)",

Refactoring complete. Summary:

## Changes Made

1. **Created `views/partials/page-init.html`**
   - Uses Nunjucks conditionals based on `pageClass` from SiteConfig
   - Handles "Home", "Introduction", and default "View" cases
   - Uses `{{ basePath }}` template variable for environment-specific paths

2. **Updated `views/layouts/page.html`**
   - Replaced `{% if pageScript %}{{ pageScript | safe }}{% endif %}` with `{% include "partials/page-init.html" %}`

3. **Refactored `scripts/generate-static-pages.js`**
   - Removed `getPageInitScript()` function (86 lines removed)
   - Now passes `pageClass` from `routeConfig.class` (SiteConfig)
   - Passes `basePath` as a template variable
   - Removed `pageScript` assignment

## Benefits

- SiteConfig-driven: Uses the `class` property from `siteRoutes.js`
- Separation of concerns: Template logic lives in templates, not JavaScript
- Maintainable: Script changes don't require modifying the build script
- Consistent: Follows the existing partial pattern (`scripts.html`, `footer.html`, etc.)
- Cleaner: Removed 86 lines of string concatenation code

## Verification

To test the changes:

```bash
# Test development mode
bun run generate:pages

# Test production mode  
NODE_ENV=production bun run generate:pages
```

The generated pages should include the correct initialization scripts based on the `class` property in SiteConfig, and the template logic is now visible and maintainable in the Nunjucks partial.

        "contents": "This aligns with functional programming principles where functions return values rather than relying on side effects (though side effects like registry updates can still exist).\n\n\n\n# Code Changes\n\nThe code stores pages in the registry and then retrieves them, which is redundant. Here's a cleaner approach:\n\n## Recommendation: Return page instances directly\n\n**Current pattern (problematic):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Function sets in registry\ninitializePage(pageTemplate) {\n  const page = new pageClass(...);\n  this.pageRegistry.setCurrentPage(page); // Store\n  // No return\n}\n\n// Caller has to retrieve\nawait this.pageLoader.initializePage(template);\nconst page = this.pageRegistry.getCurrentPage(); // Retrieve again\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Better pattern:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Function returns the instance\ninitializePage(pageTemplate) {\n  const pageClass = this.pageRegistry.getPage(pageTemplate);\n  const page = new pageClass(...);\n  this.pageRegistry.setCurrentPage(page); // Still store for registry access\n  return page; // But also return it\n}\n\n// Caller uses directly\nconst page = await this.pageLoader.initializePage(template);\nawait page.create();\nawait page.show();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Suggested Refactoring:\n\n1. **&#96;initializePage()&#96; should return the page instance:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\ninitializePage(pageTemplate) {\n  const pageClass = this.pageRegistry.getPage(pageTemplate);\n  const elementSelector = &#96;main[data-template=\"${pageTemplate}\"]&#96;;\n  const page = new pageClass({\n    element: elementSelector,\n    smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll,\n    transitionManager: this.transitionManager,\n    footnotes: this.footnotes,\n  });\n  \n  this.pageRegistry.setCurrentPage(page); // Store for other parts of app\n  return page; // Return for immediate use\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. **&#96;setupPages()&#96; should return the page instance:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync setupPages(specificPage = null) {\n  // ... existing logic ...\n  ",

        "contents": "export default class Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    this.id = id;\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.selectorChildren = elements;\n    this._created = false;\n    this._destroyed = false;\n  }\n  \n  async create() {\n    if (this._created) return;\n    this._created = true;\n    \n    // Base initialization\n    this.element = $(this.selector);\n    this.elements = pageObject(this.selectorChildren);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before components created\n    await this.onBeforeCreate?.();\n    \n    // Base component setup\n    this.smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n    this.footnotes = new Footnotes({smoothScroll: this.smoothScroll});\n    this.createAnimations();\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After components created\n    await this.onAfterCreate?.();\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    if (!this.smoothScroll.enabled() &amp;&amp; !this.preloader) {\n      this.smoothScroll.create();\n      this.smoothScroll.scrollTo(0, {immediate: true});\n    }\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before transition\n    await this.onBeforeShow?.();\n    \n    await this.animation.GSAPHideTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After transition\n    await this.onAfterShow?.();\n  }\n  \n  async hide(route) {\n    // ✅ Hook: Before transition\n    await this.onBeforeHide?.(route);\n    \n    await this.transitionManager.getTransition(route);\n    await this.animation.GSAPShowTransition(this.transitionOverlay);\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After transition, before destroy\n    await this.onAfterHide?.(route);\n    \n    this.destroy();\n  }\n  \n  destroy() {\n    if (this._destroyed) return;\n    this._destroyed = true;\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: Before cleanup\n    this.onBeforeDestroy?.();\n    \n    this.removeEventListeners();\n    if (this.smoothScroll) {\n      this.smoothScroll.destroy();\n      this.smoothScroll = null;\n    }\n    \n    // ✅ Hook: After cleanup\n    this.onAfterDestroy?.();\n  }\n  \n  // Hook methods (optional, subclasses can override)\n  async onBeforeCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterCreate() {} // Optional\n  async onBeforeShow() {} // Optional\n  async onAfterShow() {} // Optional",

        },
        "contents": "async function generateStaticPages() {\n\n          }\n          // Add page class from SiteConfig to drive template logic\n          if (routeConfig.class) {\n            templateData.pageClass = routeConfig.class;\n          }\n          // Add transition data for overlay (image and alt only, no copy)\n          if (routeConfig.transition) {\n            templateData.transitionImage = routeConfig.transition.image;\n            templateData.transitionAlt = routeConfig.transition.alt;\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      \n      // Fallback defaults if no transition data\n      if (!templateData.transitionImage) {\n        templateData.transitionImage = \"https://shea-memorandum-site.b-cdn.net/images/home-theme-desktop.webp\";\n        templateData.transitionAlt = \"The Shea Memorandum Logo\";\n      }\n      \n      // Generate preload link for transition image to ensure browser cache\n      templateData.transitionPreloadLink = &#96;&lt;link rel=\"preload\" as=\"image\" href=\"${templateData.transitionImage}\" crossorigin=\"anonymous\"&gt;&#96;;\n\n      // Render the template with environment-specific asset paths and page title\n      let rendered = nunjucks.render(&#96;pages/${file}&#96;, templateData);\n\n      if (isProduction) {\n        rendered = await minify(rendered, {\n          collapseWhitespace: true,\n          removeComments: true,\n          removeRedundantAttributes: true,\n          useShortDoctype: true,\n          minifyCSS: true,\n          minifyJS: true,\n          removeEmptyAttributes: true,\n          removeOptionalTags: true,\n          removeScriptTypeAttributes: true,\n          removeStyleLinkTypeAttributes: true,\n          sortAttributes: true,\n          sortClassName: true,\n        });\n      }\n\n      await Bun.write(outputPath, rendered);\n\n      console.log(\n        &#96;✓ Generated ${file} → ${outputPath.replace(outputDir.pathname, \"\")} (${isProduction ? \"production\" : \"development\"} mode)&#96;\n      );\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "// App.js - Creates and shares services\nclass App {\n  constructor() {\n    // ✅ Create shared services once\n    this.registry = new Registry();\n    this.transitionManager = new TransitionManager({ registry: this.registry });\n    this.router = new Router({ registry: this.registry });\n    \n    // ✅ Store in services object for easy access\n    this.services = {\n      registry: this.registry,\n      transitionManager: this.transitionManager,\n      router: this.router,\n      // Will create others as needed\n    };\n  }\n  \n  async loadAndCreatePage(template) {\n    const PageClass = await this.loadPageClass(template);\n    \n    // ✅ Inject shared services\n    this.currentPage = new PageClass({\n      id: template,\n      element: \"main\",\n      transitionManager: this.services.transitionManager,\n      // smoothScroll will be created per-page (or shared if preferred)\n    });\n    \n    await this.currentPage.create();\n  }\n}\n\n// Page.js - Accepts injected services\nexport default class Page {\n  constructor({ \n    id, \n    element, \n    elements,\n    // ✅ Injected services (shared, stateful)\n    transitionManager,\n    // ✅ Optional - can create if not provided\n    smoothScroll = null,\n    animation = null,\n  }) {\n    this.id = id;\n    this.selector = element;\n    this.transitionManager = transitionManager; // Shared instance\n    \n    // ✅ Stateless utilities can be instantiated\n    this.animation = animation ?? new Animation();\n    \n    // ✅ Per-page services (create if not injected)\n    this.smoothScroll = smoothScroll;\n  }\n  \n  async create() {\n    // ✅ Use shared transition manager\n    // (images already preloaded by first page!)\n    await this.transitionManager.getTransition(route);\n    \n    // ✅ Create per-page service if not injected\n    if (!this.smoothScroll) {\n      this.smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Pros and Cons Comparison\n\n### ES6 Imports\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Simple, straightforward\n- ✅ No boilerplate\n- ✅ IDE can track imports easily\n- ✅ Tree-shaking works well\n- ✅ Great for utilities\n\n**Cons:**\n- ❌ Hard to mock in tests",

        "contents": "import { Preloader } from \"./components/Preloader.js\";\nimport { Navigation } from \"./components/Navigation.js\";\nimport { $, setupHelpers } from \"./utils/Helpers.js\";\nimport { liveReload, setupPageConfig } from \"./utils/Environment.js\";\n\nclass App {\n  /**\n   * Constructor: Configuration only (pure, no side effects)\n   */\n  constructor() {\n    // ✅ Configuration: Setup page config\n    this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig();\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Store references (no DOM lookup)\n    this.pageHistory = window.history;\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Initialize state containers\n    this.pages = new Map();\n    \n    // ✅ Configuration: Initialize flags\n    this._initialized = false;\n    \n    // ❌ NO side effects\n    // ❌ NO DOM access\n    // ❌ NO async operations\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Initialize application (side effects, DOM access, async)\n   * Call this after constructor\n   */\n  async init() {\n    if (this._initialized) {\n      console.warn('App.init() called multiple times');\n      return;\n    }\n    this._initialized = true;\n    \n    // 1. Setup helpers (modifies prototypes)\n    setupHelpers();\n    \n    // 2. Create services\n    this.createServices();\n    \n    // 3. Setup pages (async, DOM access)\n    await this.setupPages();\n    \n    // 4. Setup app event listeners\n    this.setupApp();\n    this.setupEventListeners();\n    \n    // 5. Create preloader\n    this.createPreloader();\n    \n    // 6. Enable hot reload\n    liveReload();\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Create the services for the application\n   */\n  createServices() {\n    this.services = createServices();\n    this.registry = this.services.registry;\n    this.router = this.services.router;\n    this.smoothScroll = this.services.smoothScroll;\n    this.transitionManager = this.services.transitionManager;\n  }\n  \n  /**\n   * Set up app event listeners and router\n   */\n  setupApp() {\n    // ✅ Guard DOM ready state",

        "contents": "- Focus on testable classes first\n- Use best practice for new code\n\nThe goal isn't perfection - it's maintainable, testable code that works well over time.\n\n\n## Your Observation: It Works!\n\nYou're absolutely right!       "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./documentation/guides/COMPONENT_GUIDE.md",

        },
        "contents": "5. Override points: Subclasses can override specific phases\n6. Aligns with lifecycle guide: Follows the documented patterns\n\n---\n\n## Additional Considerations\n\n### Error Handling\nEach function can return a boolean or throw, allowing &#96;create()&#96; to handle failures:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync create() {\n  if (this._created) return;\n  \n  try {\n    await this.beforeCreate?.();\n    \n    if (!(await this.mount())) {\n      throw new Error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Mount failed&#96;);\n    }\n    \n    await this.initComponents();\n    this.initAnimations();\n    await this.ready();\n    \n    this._created = true;\n    await this.afterCreate?.();\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Creation failed:&#96;, error);\n    // Cleanup partial creation if needed\n    throw error; // Let parent handle\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n# Separating Configuration from Initialization in App.js\n\n## Current Problem\n\nYour constructor is doing too much:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nconstructor() {\n  setupHelpers();              // Side effect (modifies prototype)\n  this.createServices();        // Creates state\n  this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig(); // Configuration (okay)\n  this.setupPages();           // DOM access, async operations\n  this.setupApp();             // Event listeners\n  this.setupEventListeners();  // Event listeners\n  this.createPreloader();      // Creates components\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Issues:**\n1. ❌ Mixing configuration and initialization\n2. ❌ Side effects in constructor\n3. ❌ Async operations (&#96;setupPages()&#96; is async but not awaited)\n4. ❌ Hard to test\n5. ❌ Can't create instance without initializing\n\n---\n\n## Solution: Two-Phase Initialization\n\n### Pattern: Constructor (Config) + init() (Initialization)\n\n**Phase 1: Constructor - Configuration Only**\n- Store configuration\n- Accept dependencies\n- No side effects\n- No DOM access\n- No async operations\n\n**Phase 2: init() - Initialization**\n- All side effects\n- DOM access\n- Async operations\n- Creates components\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Approach\n\n### Option 1: init() Method (Recommended)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "5. Override points: Subclasses can override specific phases",
            "lineNumber": 858
          },
          {
            "text": "6. Aligns with lifecycle guide: Follows the documented patterns",
            "lineNumber": 859
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 860
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 861
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 862
          },
          {
            "text": "## Additional Considerations",
            "lineNumber": 863
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 864
          },
          {
            "text": "### Error Handling",
            "lineNumber": 865
          },
          {
            "text": "Each function can return a boolean or throw, allowing &#96;create()&#96; to handle failures:",
            "lineNumber": 866
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 867
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript",
            "lineNumber": 868
          },
          {
            "text": "async create() {",
            "lineNumber": 869
          },
          {
            "text": "  if (this._created) return;",
            "lineNumber": 870
          },
          {
            "text": "  ",
            "lineNumber": 871
          },
          {
            "text": "  try {",
            "lineNumber": 872
          },
          {
            "text": "    await this.beforeCreate?.();",
            "lineNumber": 873
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 874
          },
          {
            "text": "    if (!(await this.mount())) {",
            "lineNumber": 875
          },
          {
            "text": "      throw new Error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Mount failed&#96;);",
            "lineNumber": 876
          },
          {
            "text": "    }",
            "lineNumber": 877
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 878
          },
          {
            "text": "    await this.initComponents();",
            "lineNumber": 879
          },
          {
            "text": "    this.initAnimations();",
            "lineNumber": 880
          },
          {
            "text": "    await this.ready();",
            "lineNumber": 881
          },
          {
            "text": "    ",
            "lineNumber": 882
          },
          {
            "text": "    this._created = true;",
            "lineNumber": 883
          },
          {
            "text": "    await this.afterCreate?.();",
            "lineNumber": 884
          },
          {
            "text": "  } catch (error) {",
            "lineNumber": 885
          },
          {
            "text": "    console.error(&#96;Page ${this.id}: Creation failed:&#96;, error);",
            "lineNumber": 886
          },
          {
            "text": "    // Cleanup partial creation if needed",
            "lineNumber": 887
          },
          {
            "text": "    throw error; // Let parent handle",
            "lineNumber": 888
          },
          {
            "text": "  }",
            "lineNumber": 889
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 890
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 891
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 892
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 893
          },
          {
            "text": "# Separating Configuration from Initialization in App.js",
            "lineNumber": 894
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 895
          },
          {
            "text": "## Current Problem",
            "lineNumber": 896
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 897
          },
          {
            "text": "Your constructor is doing too much:",
            "lineNumber": 898
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 899
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 900
          },
          {
            "text": "constructor() {",
            "lineNumber": 901
          },
          {
            "text": "  setupHelpers();              // Side effect (modifies prototype)",
            "lineNumber": 902
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.createServices();        // Creates state",
            "lineNumber": 903
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.pageConfig = setupPageConfig(); // Configuration (okay)",
            "lineNumber": 904
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.setupPages();           // DOM access, async operations",
            "lineNumber": 905
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.setupApp();             // Event listeners",
            "lineNumber": 906
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.setupEventListeners();  // Event listeners",
            "lineNumber": 907
          },
          {
            "text": "  this.createPreloader();      // Creates components",
            "lineNumber": 908
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 909
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 910
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 911
          },
          {
            "text": "**Issues:**",
            "lineNumber": 912
          },
          {
            "text": "1. ❌ Mixing configuration and initialization",
            "lineNumber": 913
          },
          {
            "text": "2. ❌ Side effects in constructor",
            "lineNumber": 914
          },
          {
            "text": "3. ❌ Async operations (&#96;setupPages()&#96; is async but not awaited)",
            "lineNumber": 915
          },
          {
            "text": "4. ❌ Hard to test",
            "lineNumber": 916
          },
          {
            "text": "5. ❌ Can't create instance without initializing",
            "lineNumber": 917
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 918
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 919
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 920
          },
          {
            "text": "## Solution: Two-Phase Initialization",
            "lineNumber": 921
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 922
          },
          {
            "text": "### Pattern: Constructor (Config) + init() (Initialization)",
            "lineNumber": 923
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 924
          },
          {
            "text": "**Phase 1: Constructor - Configuration Only**",
            "lineNumber": 925
          },
          {
            "text": "- Store configuration",
            "lineNumber": 926
          },
          {
            "text": "- Accept dependencies",
            "lineNumber": 927
          },
          {
            "text": "- No side effects",
            "lineNumber": 928
          },
          {
            "text": "- No DOM access",
            "lineNumber": 929
          },
          {
            "text": "- No async operations",
            "lineNumber": 930
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 931
          },
          {
            "text": "**Phase 2: init() - Initialization**",
            "lineNumber": 932
          },
          {
            "text": "- All side effects",
            "lineNumber": 933
          },
          {
            "text": "- DOM access",
            "lineNumber": 934
          },
          {
            "text": "- Async operations",
            "lineNumber": 935
          },
          {
            "text": "- Creates components",
            "lineNumber": 936
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 937
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 938
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 939
          },
          {
            "text": "## Recommended Approach",
            "lineNumber": 940
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 941
          },
          {
            "text": "### Option 1: init() Method (Recommended)",
            "lineNumber": 942
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 943
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;js",
            "lineNumber": 944
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.3617297410964966
    },

No hooks needed, uses parent implementation\nexport class View extends Page {\n  constructor({ id, element, elements }) {\n    super({ id, element, elements });\n  }\n  // ✅ Doesn't need to define anything - uses parent's show/hide\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Composition vs Inheritance\n\n### Current: Inheritance\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nclass Page {\n  async show() { /* ... */ }\n}\n\nclass Home extends Page {\n  // Home IS-A Page\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Alternative: Composition\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Page is a composition of behaviors\nclass Page {\n  constructor(behaviors = {}) {\n    this.showBehavior = behaviors.show || new DefaultShowBehavior();\n    this.hideBehavior = behaviors.hide || new DefaultHideBehavior();\n  }\n  \n  async show() {\n    await this.showBehavior.execute(this);\n  }\n}\n\n// Home uses composition\nclass Home {\n  constructor() {\n    super({\n      show: new HomeShowBehavior(), // Custom behavior\n      hide: new DefaultHideBehavior(), // Default behavior\n    });\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Inheritance vs Composition Comparison\n\n### Inheritance (Current Approach)\n\n**Pros:**\n- ✅ Simple -         "contents": "Router.afterPageUpdate(newPage, routeInfo)\n    ├── newPage.create()\n    │   ├── createElements()\n    │   ├── createComponents()\n    │   ├── createPageAnimations()\n    │   └── setupEventListeners()\n    └── newPage.show()\n        ├── TransitionsManager.hidePageTransition()\n        └── SmoothScroll.scrollTo(0)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Page Lifecycle Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage Creation:\ncreate() → beforeCreate → createElements → createComponents → \ncreatePageAnimations → createPage → afterCreate\n\nPage Display:\nshow() → beforeShow → hidePageTransition → scrollTo(0) → afterShow\n\nPage Hiding:\nhide(route) → beforeHide → updateTransitionOverlay → \nshowPageTransition → destroy() → afterHide\n\nPage Destruction:\ndestroy() → beforeDestroy → destroyPageAnimations → \nremoveEventListeners → destroyComponents → destroyElements → afterDestroy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Animation Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage.create()\n    ↓\nPage.createPageAnimations()\n    ↓\nAnimationsManager.createPageAnimations(pageElement)\n    ├── Find elements with [data-animation]\n    ├── Group by animation type\n    ├── Create animation instances\n    └── Setup shared IntersectionObserver\n    ↓\nIntersectionObserver detects viewport entry\n    ↓\nAnimation.animateIn() (e.g., Titles.animateIn())\n    ↓\nGSAP timeline animates element\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Key Components\n\n### Router (&#96;app/services/Router.js&#96;)\n- Handles navigation lifecycle\n- Delegates route validation to RouterResolver\n- Coordinates page hiding/showing\n- Manages browser history via RouterHistory\n\n### PageLoader (&#96;app/services/PageLoader.js&#96;)\n- Dynamically loads page classes\n- Caches loaded classes in PageRegistry\n- Initializes page instances with dependencies\n- Handles first page load\n\n### PageManager (&#96;app/services/PageManager.js&#96;)\n- Fetches page HTML via fetch()\n- Updates DOM with new page content\n- Extracts page metadata (template, background, color)\n- Preloads images before page display\n\n### PageRegistry (&#96;app/services/PageRegistry.js&#96;)\n- Registry of page classes (template → PageClass)",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// In SiteConfig\n'my-section': {\n  template: \"my-section\",\n  class: \"View\",  // Use View class\n  // ... rest of config\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;View&#96; class handles all standard page functionality automatically.\n\n### Step 4: Generate Static HTML\n\nAfter creating your template, generate the static HTML:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nbun run build:html:dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis generates &#96;pages/my-new-page.html&#96; from your Nunjucks template.\n\n### Step 5: Test Your Page\n\n1. Start the development server: &#96;bun run dev&#96;\n2. Navigate to &#96;http://localhost:3000/my-new-page&#96;\n3. Verify:\n   - Page loads correctly\n   - Transitions work\n   - Animations trigger\n   - Images load\n   - Navigation links work\n\n## Page Registry Setup\n\nThe Page Registry automatically manages page classes. Here's how it works:\n\n### Automatic Registration\n\nPages are registered automatically when first loaded:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// PageLoader.loadPage() automatically:\n1. Checks if page class is already in registry\n2. If not, dynamically imports the page class\n3. Stores it in PageRegistry.pages Map\n4. Returns the class for instantiation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Manual Registration (Advanced)\n\nYou can manually register pages if needed:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// In your code\nconst MyPageClass = await import('./pages/MyPage.js');\npageRegistry.setPage('my-page', MyPageClass.default);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Checking Page Status\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Check if page is registered\nif (pageRegistry.hasPage('my-page')) {\n  const PageClass = pageRegistry.getPage('my-page');\n}\n\n// Get current page instance\nconst currentPage = pageRegistry.getCurrentPage();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Animation System\n\nThe animation system uses data attributes to automatically discover and animate elements.\n\n### Using Built-in Animations\n\n#### Title Animation\n\nAdd &#96;data-animation=\"title\"&#96; to any element:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;h1 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;Animated Title&lt;/h1&gt;\n&lt;h2 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;Another Animated Title&lt;/h2&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;Titles&#96; animation class will:\n- Fade in when the element enters the viewport\n- Use IntersectionObserver for performance\n- Automatically clean up on page destroy\n\n**How it works:**",

        "contents": "export function createServices() {\n  const siteConfig = new SiteConfig();\n  const animationsManager = new AnimationsManager();\n  const transitionsManager = new TransitionsManager({ siteConfig });\n  const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();\n  const footnotes = new Footnotes({ smoothScroll });\n  const pageLoader = new PageLoader({ siteConfig, smoothScroll, animationsManager, transitionsManager, footnotes });\n  const pageRegistry = new PageRegistry({ siteConfig, pageLoader });\n  // ... more services\n  \n  return {\n    siteConfig,\n    router,\n    smoothScroll,\n    animationsManager,\n    // ... all services\n  };\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Design Patterns\n\n### 1. Service Factory Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/ServiceFactory.js&#96;\n\nCreates and configures all application services with proper dependency injection. Services are created once and shared across the application.\n\n### 2. Registry Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/services/PageRegistry.js&#96;\n\nThe &#96;PageRegistry&#96; maintains a registry of page classes and their instances. It tracks:\n- Loaded page classes (Map of template → PageClass)\n- Current page instance\n- Current page template\n\n**Usage:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Register a page class\npageRegistry.setPage('home', Home);\n\n// Get a page class\nconst HomeClass = pageRegistry.getPage('home');\n\n// Track current page\npageRegistry.setCurrentPage(pageInstance);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Manager Pattern\nMultiple managers coordinate specific domains:\n\n- **PageManager** (&#96;app/services/PageManager.js&#96;): Manages page content updates, DOM manipulation, and page metadata\n- **AnimationsManager** (&#96;app/animations/AnimationsManager.js&#96;): Manages page animations lifecycle, IntersectionObserver setup, and animation cleanup\n- **TransitionsManager** (&#96;app/animations/TransitionsManager.js&#96;): Manages page transition overlays, image preloading, and transition templates\n\n### 4. Component Base Class Pattern\n**Location:** &#96;app/components/Component.js&#96;\n\nAll components inherit from a base &#96;Component&#96; class that provides:\n- Event management (via EventManager)\n- Element selection and caching",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "export function createServices() {",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "  const siteConfig = new SiteConfig();",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "  const animationsManager = new AnimationsManager();",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "  const transitionsManager = new TransitionsManager({ siteConfig });",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "  const smoothScroll = new SmoothScroll();",
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "  const footnotes = new Footnotes({ smoothScroll });",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "  const pageLoader = new PageLoader({ siteConfig, smoothScroll, animationsManager, transitionsManager, footnotes });",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {

{
  "plan": "# Fix Page Subclass create() Methods\n\n## Problem Analysis\n\nThe &#96;Page&#96; superclass defines an &#96;async create()&#96; method that orchestrates the page initialization lifecycle:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nasync create() {\n  await this.beforeCreate?.()\n  await this.createElements();    \n  await this.createComponents();\n  this.createPageAnimations();\n  this.createPage();\n  this._created = true;\n  await this.afterCreate?.()\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nHowever, all subclasses are not properly extending this pattern:\n\n### Issues Found:\n\n1. **Home.js** (line 17-20):\n   - &#96;create()&#96; is not declared as &#96;async&#96;\n   - Does not &#96;await super.create()&#96;\n   - Passes unnecessary &#96;{}&#96; argument to &#96;super.create()&#96; (which takes no parameters)\n   - Calls &#96;this.setup()&#96; immediately without awaiting superclass initialization\n\n2. **View.js** (line 24-26):\n   - &#96;create()&#96; is not declared as &#96;async&#96;\n   - Does not &#96;await super.create()&#96;\n   - Passes unnecessary &#96;{}&#96; argument\n\n3. **Introduction.js** (line 13-15):\n   - &#96;create()&#96; is not declared as &#96;async&#96;\n   - Does not &#96;await super.create()&#96;\n   - Passes unnecessary &#96;{}&#96; argument\n\n4. **References.js** (line 13-15):\n   - &#96;create()&#96; is not declared as &#96;async&#96;\n   - Does not &#96;await super.create()&#96;\n   - Passes unnecessary &#96;{}&#96; argument\n\n## Impact\n\n- Race conditions: Subclass logic may execute before superclass initialization completes\n- The &#96;_created&#96; flag may not be set before subclass methods access page state\n- &#96;Home.setup()&#96; may run before elements/components are initialized\n- Promise chains are broken, causing potential unhandled promise rejections\n\n## Solution\n\nUpdate all subclass &#96;create()&#96; methods to:\n1. Declare as &#96;async&#96;\n2. &#96;await super.create()&#96; (no arguments needed)\n3. Place subclass-specific logic after the await\n\n## Files to Modify\n\n### 1. &#96;app/pages/Home.js&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Current (WRONG):\ncreate() {\n  super.create({});\n  this.setup();\n}\n\n// Fixed:\nasync create() {\n  await super.create();\n  this.setup();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. &#96;app/pages/View.js&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Current (WRONG):\ncreate() {\n  super.create({});\n}\n\n// Fixed:\nasync create() {\n  await super.create();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. &#96;app/pages/Introduction.js&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Current (WRONG):\ncreate() {\n  super.create({});\n}\n\n// Fixed:\nasync create() {\n  await super.create();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 4. &#96;app/pages/References.js&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\n// Current (WRONG):\ncreate() {\n  super.create({});\n}\n\n// Fixed:\nasync create() {\n  await super.create();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Verification\n\nAfter changes, verify:\n- All &#96;create()&#96; methods are &#96;async&#96;\n- All &#96;super.create()&#96; calls are &#96;await&#96;ed\n- No arguments passed to &#96;super.create()&#96;\n- Template initialization scripts (&#96;views/partials/page-init.html&#96;) already correctly &#96;await page.create()&#96;, so no changes needed there\n\n## Benefits\n\n- Proper async/await chain ensures superclass initialization completes before subclass logic\n- Eliminates race conditions\n- Ensures &#96;_created&#96; flag is set before subclass methods run\n- Maintains proper Promise handling",

The issue: `View.show()` overrides `Page.show()` without calling `super.show()`, and it's not `async` while the template `await`s it. The parent `show()` handles smoothScroll setup, so that logic never runs.

Fixing by making `View.show()` `async` and calling `await super.show()` first:


---

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="edit_file_v2">

<details><summary>Tool use: **edit_file_v2** • Edit file: /Users/nickname/Documents/code-design/frontend-web-app/app/pages/View.js</summary>

</details>

</tool-use>

---


Fixed. The issue was:

1. **`View.show()` wasn't `async`** — The template calls `await page.show()`, but the method wasn't async, so the await didn't work correctly.
2. **Missing `super.show()` call** — The parent `Page.show()` method is `async` and contains important logic (smoothScroll setup), which wasn't being executed.

The fix:
- Made `View.show()` `async` to match the parent signature
- Added `await super.show()` to ensure the parent's smoothScroll logic runs first
- Then executes your custom `console.log`

This follows the same pattern as the `create()` methods we just fixed — always `await` the superclass method first to maintain the proper initialization chain. The console.log should now appear in the browser console.

No. In JavaScript, overriding a method replaces the parent method; it doesn't automatically call the superclass version. You must explicitly call `super.methodName()` to invoke the parent.

Here's how it works:

In JavaScript, overriding a method replaces the parent method; it doesn't automatically call the superclass version. You must explicitly call `super.methodName()`.

## How JavaScript Method Overriding Works

When you define `show()` in `View`, it replaces `Page.show()`:

```javascript
// Without super.show():
class View extends Page {
  async show() {
    console.log("View page shown");
    // Page.show() is NEVER called - it's completely replaced!
  }
}
```

The parent `Page.show()` contains important logic:
- Calls `beforeShow?.()` hook
- Sets up smoothScroll
- Calls `afterShow?.()` hook

Without `await super.show()`, none of that runs.

## The Correct Pattern

To extend (not replace) the parent method, call `super`:

```javascript
class View extends Page {
  async show() {
    await super.show();  // ✅ Explicitly call parent method first
    console.log("View page shown");  // Then add your custom logic
  }
}
```

## Why This Matters

This is why we fixed the `create()` methods earlier — they were calling `super.create()` but not `await`ing it, which caused race conditions. The same principle applies to `show()`.

**Summary:** JavaScript doesn't auto-call superclass methods. If you override a method and need the parent's behavior, call `super.methodName()` explicitly.

        "contents": "/**\n * SiteConfig - Site-wide route mappings and page metadata\n * Harmonizes the data-template field to href, js classes and browser urls \n * Central configuration for all routes, page classes, and transition data\n */\n\nimport { siteRoutes } from './siteRoutes.js';\n\nexport class SiteConfig {\n  constructor() {\n    this.routes = {};\n    this.initializeSettings();\n  }\n\n  initializeSettings() {\n    this.settings = siteRoutes;\n  }\n\n  get(template) {\n    return this.settings[template];\n  }\n\n  getClass(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.class;\n  }\n\n  getLink(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.link;\n  }\n\n  getUrl(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.url;\n  }\n\n  getTemplate(template) {\n    return this.settings[template]?.template;\n  }\n\n  has(template) {\n    return this.settings[template] !== undefined;\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "import Page from \"./Page.js\";\n\n\n/**\n * View class for rendering a view\n * \n * Generic class for view/pages/*.html files instead of using a class for each page.\n * Extends Page and can use all lifecycle hooks.\n * \n * See &#96;documentation/guides/PAGE_LIFECYCLE.md&#96; for examples of using lifecycle hooks:\n * - Custom exit animations (beforeHide)\n * - Custom entrance animations (afterShow)\n * - Component setup and teardown (afterCreate, beforeDestroy)\n * \n * @param {Object} props - The properties for the view\n * @param {string} props.element - The element selector for the view\n * @param {Object} props.elements - Additional element selectors\n */\nexport class View extends Page {\n  constructor({ element, elements, ...options }) {\n    super({\n      element: element,\n      pageTransitionOverlay: \".page-transition-overlay\",\n      elements: { wrapper: \".page-content\", ...elements },\n      // Forward services and any other options\n      ...options,\n    });\n  }\n\n  create() {\n    super.create({});\n  }\n}",

      "codeBlock": {

        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 69

        "contents": "# Page Animation System Documentation\n\n## Overview\n\nThe animation system automatically handles page animations based on &#96;data-animation&#96; attributes in your HTML. It uses a single &#96;IntersectionObserver&#96; per page to efficiently trigger animations when elements enter or leave the viewport.\n\n**Key Components:**\n- **&#96;AnimationsManager&#96;**: Manages the animation lifecycle, auto-detects animated elements, and coordinates a shared IntersectionObserver\n- **&#96;Titles&#96;**: Animation class that fades in title elements when they enter the viewport\n- **Page Integration**: &#96;Page.js&#96; calls the manager during create/destroy lifecycle\n\n## How to Set Up a Page Animation\n\n### Step 1: Add &#96;data-animation&#96; Attribute to HTML\n\nSimply add the &#96;data-animation&#96; attribute to any element you want to animate:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;h2 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;My Animated Title&lt;/h2&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe attribute value (&#96;\"title\"&#96;) corresponds to an animation class registered in the &#96;AnimationsManager&#96; registry.\n\n### Step 2: Register Animation Class (if creating new type)\n\nIf you're creating a new animation type (e.g., &#96;\"image\"&#96;), add it to the registry in &#96;AnimationsManager.js&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nthis.animationRegistry = {\n  title: Titles,\n  image: Images,  // New animation type\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: Create Animation Class (if new type)\n\nCreate a new animation class (e.g., &#96;Images.js&#96;) that follows the same pattern as &#96;Titles.js&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nexport class Images {\n  constructor(element) {\n    this.element = element;\n    this.animationTimelines = [];\n  }\n\n  animateIn() {\n    // Animation logic when element enters viewport\n  }\n\n  animateOut() {\n    // Animation logic when element leaves viewport\n  }\n\n  kill() {\n    // Cleanup all timelines\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Automatic Setup\n\nThe system automatically:\n- Detects elements with &#96;data-animation&#96; attributes when the page is created\n- Creates animation instances for each element\n- Sets up a shared IntersectionObserver\n- Triggers animations when elements enter/leave the viewport\n\n**No additional code needed in &#96;Page.js&#96;** - it's all handled automatically!",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "/**\n * Constants for the application\n * Prevent the use of \"magic strings\" by providing a single source of truth for all selectors, attributes, events, and other constants used across the app\n * Wrap objects in Object.freeze() to prevent mutation outside of this class\n *\n * Problems with \"magic strings\":\n * - Typos not caught until runtime\n * - Hard to refactor (change selector? search entire codebase!)\n * - No single source of truth\n * - Easy to miss when updating\n */\n\n/**\n * CSS selectors\n */\nexport const SELECTORS = Object.freeze({\n  // Main structure\n  MAIN: \"main\",\n  MAIN_WITH_TEMPLATE: \"main[data-template]\",\n  BODY: \"body\",\n\n  // Preloader\n  PRELOADER: \".preloader\",\n  PRELOADER_TITLE: \".preloader h1\",\n  PRELOADER_COUNTER: \".preloader-counter\",\n  PRELOADER_COPY: \".preloader-transition-copy h1\",\n  PRELOADER_COPY_CONTAINER: \".preloader-transition-copy\",\n  PRELOADER_IMAGE: \"img[data-src].preloader-transition-image__img\",\n\n  // Page transitions\n  TRANSITION_OVERLAY: \".page-transition-overlay\",\n  TRANSITION_TEMPLATES: \"#page-transition-overlay-templates\",\n  TRANSITION_COPY: \".page-transition-overlay__copy\",\n  TRANSITION_IMAGE: \".page-transition-overlay__image\",\n\n\n  // Footnotes\n  FOOTNOTES: \"ul.footnotes li\",\n  SUPERSCRIPT_LINKS: \".page-content a.footnote-superscript-link\",\n  SUPERSCRIPT_LINK: \"a.footnote-superscript-link\",\n  FOOTNOTE_LINK: \"a.footnote-link\",\n\n\n  // Navigation\n  NAV: \"nav\",\n  NAV_LINKS: \"nav a\",\n  LINK: \".link\",\n  INTERNAL_LINK: \"a.internal-link\",\n  NAV_TOGGLE: \".navigation__toggle\",\n  NAV_TITLE: \".navigation__title\",\n\n  // Page content\n  PAGE_CONTENT: \"section.page-template\",\n\n  // Images\n  LAZY_IMAGES: \"img[data-src]\",\n\n  // Animations\n  ANIMATIONS_ATTRIBUTE: \"[data-animation]\",\n  TITLE_ANIMATIONS: '[data-animation=\"title\"]',\n  \n  // HTML elements\n  TEMPLATE: \"template\",\n  IMG: \"img\",\n});\n\n/**\n * HTML attribute names\n */\nexport const ATTRIBUTES = Object.freeze\n;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./app/animations/README.animations.md",

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 134
          }
        },
        "contents": "**No additional code needed in &#96;Page.js&#96;** - it's all handled automatically!\n\n## How AnimationsManager Coordinates Animations\n\n### Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;AnimationsManager&#96; uses a factory pattern with a registry to manage animations:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nPage.js\n  └─&gt; AnimationsManager.createPageAnimations(pageElement)\n       ├─&gt; validatePageElement()          [Validates input]\n       ├─&gt; findAnimatedElements()         [Discovers elements]\n       ├─&gt; groupElementsByType()          [Groups by type]\n       ├─&gt; createAnimationInstances()     [Creates instances]\n       └─&gt; createSharedIntersectionObserver() [Sets up observer]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step-by-Step Process\n\n#### 1. Page Creation (&#96;Page.create()&#96; → &#96;createPageAnimations()&#96;)\n\nWhen a page is created, &#96;Page.js&#96; calls:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nthis.animationsManager.createPageAnimations(this.element);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2. Cleanup Previous Page (&#96;destroyPageAnimations()&#96;)\n\nFirst, any existing animations from the previous page are cleaned up:\n- Kills all animation timelines\n- Disconnects the previous IntersectionObserver\n- Resets the &#96;pageAnimations&#96; array\n\n#### 3. Validation (&#96;validatePageElement()&#96;)\n\nValidates that the page element is a valid HTMLElement. Throws an error if invalid.\n\n#### 4. Discovery (&#96;findAnimatedElements()&#96;)\n\nSearches the page for all elements with &#96;data-animation&#96; attributes:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\npageElement.querySelectorAll('[data-animation]')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nReturns a &#96;NodeList&#96; of elements to animate.\n\n#### 5. Grouping (&#96;groupElementsByType()&#96;)\n\nGroups elements by their animation type into a &#96;Map&#96;:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nMap {\n  'title' =&gt; [element1, element2, ...],\n  'image' =&gt; [element3, element4, ...]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis allows batch creation of the same animation type.\n\n#### 6. Instance Creation (&#96;createAnimationInstances()&#96;)\n\nFor each animation type:\n- Looks up the animation class from the registry\n- Creates an instance for each element\n- Registers each instance in &#96;this.pageAnimations&#96; for tracking\n- Returns an array of all created instances",
        "signatures": {},

      "codeBlock": {

        "range": {

        "contents": "- Returns an array of all created instances\n\n#### 7. Observer Setup (&#96;createSharedIntersectionObserver()&#96;)\n\nCreates a single &#96;IntersectionObserver&#96; for all animations:\n- Disconnects any previous observer\n- Creates a new observer with a callback that:\n  - Finds the animation instance for each intersecting element\n  - Calls &#96;animateIn()&#96; when element enters viewport\n  - Calls &#96;animateOut()&#96; when element leaves viewport\n- Observes all animated elements\n\n#### 8. Page Destruction (&#96;Page.destroy()&#96; → &#96;destroyPageAnimations()&#96;)\n\nWhen navigating away, &#96;Page.js&#96; calls:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;javascript\nthis.animationsManager.destroyPageAnimations();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis:\n- Calls &#96;kill()&#96; on all registered animation instances\n- Disconnects the IntersectionObserver\n- Resets the &#96;pageAnimations&#96; array\n\n## Key Design Patterns\n\n### 1. Single IntersectionObserver Pattern\n\nInstead of creating one observer per element, a single shared observer watches all animated elements. This is much more performant, especially with many animations.\n\n### 2. Registry Pattern\n\nAnimation types are registered in &#96;animationRegistry&#96;, making it easy to add new types without modifying core logic.\n\n### 3. Factory Pattern\n\n&#96;createAnimationInstances()&#96; acts as a factory, creating instances based on the registry mapping.\n\n### 4. Pure Functions\n\nThe refactored code uses pure functions (&#96;validatePageElement&#96;, &#96;findAnimatedElements&#96;, &#96;groupElementsByType&#96;) that:\n- Have no side effects\n- Return predictable outputs\n- Are easily testable\n\n## Animation Instance Lifecycle\n\nEach animation instance (e.g., &#96;Titles&#96;) follows this lifecycle:\n\n1. **Construction**: Element is passed to constructor, timelines array is initialized\n2. **Registration**: Instance is added to &#96;AnimationsManager.pageAnimations&#96;\n3. **Observation**: Element is observed by the shared IntersectionObserver\n4. **Animation**: &#96;animateIn()&#96; or &#96;animateOut()&#96; is called when element intersects viewport\n5. **Cleanup**: &#96;kill()&#96; is called on page destroy to clean up all timelines\n\n## Example Flow\n\n**HTML:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;main data-template=\"section-1\"&gt;\n  ",

          {
            "text": "Each animation instance (e.g., &#96;Titles&#96;) follows this lifecycle:",

        "contents": "## Example Flow\n\n**HTML:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;main data-template=\"section-1\"&gt;\n  &lt;h2 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;First Title&lt;/h2&gt;\n  &lt;h2 data-animation=\"title\"&gt;Second Title&lt;/h2&gt;\n&lt;/main&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Execution Flow:**\n1. &#96;Page.create()&#96; is called\n2. &#96;Page.createPageAnimations()&#96; calls &#96;AnimationsManager.createPageAnimations(mainElement)&#96;\n3. Manager finds 2 elements with &#96;data-animation=\"title\"&#96;\n4. Manager groups them: &#96;Map { 'title' =&gt; [h2, h2] }&#96;\n5. Manager creates 2 &#96;Titles&#96; instances, one per element\n6. Manager creates a single IntersectionObserver\n7. Observer watches both h2 elements\n8. When user scrolls and first h2 enters viewport → &#96;Titles.animateIn()&#96; is called\n9. When user navigates away → &#96;AnimationsManager.destroyPageAnimations()&#96; kills both instances\n\n## Benefits of This Architecture\n\n- **Performance**: Single observer instead of one per element\n- **Automatic**: No manual setup needed - just add &#96;data-animation&#96; attributes\n- **Extensible**: Easy to add new animation types via registry\n- **Maintainable**: Clear separation of concerns, pure functions, single responsibility\n- **Memory Safe**: Proper cleanup on page destroy prevents memory leaks",
